title: Generosity at work
tomorrow: dad's back Monday and wants double shifts. who tells him to stop?

cards: Five minutes past the end of a shift. Coat on, keys out, and the line at the register runs to the door. A coworker looks up, and the look says everything.
Most jobs have that moment. Here's an older one. Medina, a cold morning, an army on its way.
The city has decided to dig a trench across the open ground, and everyone has a stretch of it. Down in the dirt, hauling earth like the rest, is the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
A companion who saw him said the dust covered the skin of his belly.

teach.h: NO ONE TO DIG FOR THEM.
teach.b: He could have stood on the rim and pointed. He didn't. Anas, who was there, remembered people digging with their own hands, with no one to do it for them.

And the Prophet called out a line of verse over the shovels, a prayer for the diggers: the real life is the life to come, so forgive the helpers and the emigrants. The diggers sang back, promising to keep at it.

teach.h: A CALL, AND THE DIGGERS' ANSWER.
teach.b: A call, and an answer, while the dirt flew. That's generosity at work. Not a bonus.
Shoulders, time, showing up in someone else's stretch of the trench.
The Qur'an says it in Pickthall's words: "help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty."
A hadith in Sahih Muslim turns it into a promise: God is in the help of His servant as long as the servant is in the help of his brother. Notice which way that runs.
You take half a coworker's line, or untangle their report, and the report says God is helping you while you do it. Another hadith counts even lifting someone's bags onto their ride as charity.
One to tell a friend tonight: what the diggers remembered about the leader of their city was the dust on him, not a speech.

how: Hadith count helping someone with their load as charity, and masjid workdays and community projects put everyone, leaders included, on the same job.

o: giving time and effort to the people you work with
a company sharing its yearly profits with its staff
giving part of every paycheck to a local charity

games.q: who did what at the trench — tap the pairs.
p: remembered no one to dig for them
sang back, promising to keep at it
God helps you while you help

s: generosity in Islam is mostly about giving money
the trench is generosity of shoulders and time; a hadith counts lifting someone's bags as charity.
in the reports, the Prophet carried earth at the trench himself
a companion said the dust covered the skin of his belly.
the hadith says God helps you only after you finish helping
it says God is in your help as long as you're in the help of another: during, not after.

games.q: a new coworker keeps fumbling the closing checklist, and the manager has gone home. you know it cold. what fits the trench?
o: leave it; training people is the manager's job, not yours.
walk through it with them tonight, side by side.
buy them a coffee tomorrow so they feel welcome.
games.why: at the trench nobody stood on the rim. generosity at work is often getting into someone else's stretch with them.

practice: Bring to mind one person you work or study beside who is carrying a heavy stretch right now. Send them one small, specific offer: I can close tonight, I can read your version.
If you pray, you can ask that the help lands well, then sit quietly until the time is up.

wordCard.voice: Generosity at work: giving time and shoulders, not only money, to the people beside you. At the trench, the Prophet carried the earth too.

orig.note: Arabic: helping one another; the same root as 'help ye one another' in Qur'an 5:2.

carryVoice: Your line: generous at work, the way he carried earth at the trench. The shift isn't over until the line is.

sources.q: help ye one another unto righteousness and pious duty

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2834 (Anas: a cold morning at the trench, people digging with no one to do it for them; the Prophet's verse for the Ansar and Muhajirun and their answer)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4106 (al-Bara': he carried earth on the day of the trench until the dust covered the skin of his belly)
Sahih Muslim 2699 (God is in the help of His servant as long as the servant is in the help of his brother)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2989 (helping a man onto his mount or lifting his belongings onto it is charity)
